newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish casting firm Demisas to float shares.
newsitem.headline: Turkish casting firm Demisas to float shares.

text.p: Turkish iron casting company Demisas Dokum Emaye Mamulleri A.S. will float shares representing 16.67 percent of its capital in a two-day offer beginning on July 17, the company said.
The fixed price will be 9,000 lira per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share in the offer to be lead-managed by Garanti investment which will head a seven-member consortium.

Demisas will waive 100 billion lira of preemptive rights to sell them to the public when doubling its capital to 600 billion lira by issuing 100 billion lira of rights and 200 billion lira of bonuses.
Demisas produces pig castings to be used in durables and automotive industries. Its major shareholder is Turkey's leading electrolytic copper wire producer Sarkuysan with a 53.33 percent stake.

Of the 100 billion lira public offer, 40 percent will be allocated to foreign investors, 10 percent to domestic institutional investors and 20 percent to Sarkuysan group employees. The rest will be offered to domestic investors.

Demisas's assistant general manager Sadun Gulbahar said they targeted a 5.5 trillion lira turnover in 1997, up from last year's 2.32 trillion after raising annual output capacity to 45,000 tonnes in May from previous 33,000 tonnes.
"Production will be increased to 34,000 tonnes this year from 28,000 in 1996. Our target is to fully utilise our 45,000-tonne capacity in 1998," Gulbahar told Reuters.
He added that the company, which exports 80 to 85 percent of its production, plans to raise exports to $30 million this year from $20 million in 1996.
Demisas which employs 439 people in its plant based in Bilecik in northwestern Turkey, reported a 380 billion lira net profit in 1996.
